review_notes: I read the whole file. It adds no simp lemmas of its own. The long `attribute [-simp]` and `[-instance]` preamble is local and I did not judge it. I looked at the helper theorems (`mul_val_congr`, `inv_natural`, `pts_neg`, `pts_zero'`) and found no justification for tagging them simp. I read the definition of `schemeHomOverComp` and its existing simp lemma `schemeHomOverComp_coe` in Def_AlgebraicGeometry_RelativeGroupLaw.lean. The only weakness I could support is that the file bypasses this simp interface, and the interface has no identity or composition lemmas. I did not run Lean. The claim that plain `simp` closes those goals is inferred from the `@[simp]` lemma plus `Category.id_comp`, not tested. Another possible issue is the repeated manual `Spec.map_comp`/`ofHom_comp` square proofs (`hsq`, `hsqA`) written against the simp direction. I did not report it, because I am not sure about the result of `simp` there.

findings.problem: The four left_inv/right_inv goals unfold the definition `schemeHomOverComp` with `simp [GoodReductionJacobian.schemeHomOverComp]`. A canonical `@[simp]` lemma `schemeHomOverComp_coe` already states `(schemeHomOverComp ψ hψ x).1 = ψ ≫ x.1`, so plain `simp` should reduce these goals to `𝟙 _ ≫ 𝟙 _ ≫ x.1 = x.1`, which `Category.id_comp` closes. Unfolding the definition bypasses the intended simp interface and exposes the proof term inside the definition. The interface also has no `schemeHomOverComp_id` or `schemeHomOverComp_comp` lemma, so the identity and composition laws used in these round-trip proofs cannot be stated or used at the `SchemeHomOver` level. The same unfold-and-simp pattern appears four times.
findings.proposed_change: Replace each `by simp [GoodReductionJacobian.schemeHomOverComp]` with `by simp`, relying on `schemeHomOverComp_coe`. Better, add `@[simp]` lemmas next to `schemeHomOverComp`: `schemeHomOverComp_id : schemeHomOverComp (𝟙 _) h x = x` (for `h : 𝟙 _ ≫ t = t`) and `schemeHomOverComp_comp`. Then the two `Equiv` structures can be obtained from one generic equivalence `SchemeHomOver t f ≃ SchemeHomOver t' f` for `t = t'`. That generic equivalence would replace the hand-written `ψ`/`ψ'` pairs (`hψ`, `hψ'`, `hψA`, `hψA'`).
findings.benefit: The proofs would use the existing simp normal form, `ψ ≫ x.1`, instead of the definition body. They would not break if `schemeHomOverComp` changes. The duplicated 15-line Equiv blocks would shrink, and other users of `schemeHomOverComp`, such as `inv_natural` and `hptsA`, would get a simp-based way to reassociate and cancel identity restrictions.
